article.headline: Scores from last Night: Cleveland Central ends Clarksdale’s perfect start; Rosa Fort stays unbeaten
article.html:
Cleveland Central ended Clarksdale’s unbeaten girls basketball start Wednesday, winning 32–17 on the road, while Rosa Fort’s boys kept their own perfect opening intact with a 68–22 victory at Riverside. The results gave the Wolves and Wildcats matching 4–1 girls records and pushed the Lions to 4–0.

On the soccer field, Madison-Ridgeland Academy and Heritage Academy both protected unbeaten records with shutouts. MRA beat Bayou Academy 2–0 in a conference match, and Heritage edged Washington 1–0 in Columbus.

Cleveland Central takes both games at Clarksdale

The Cleveland Central girls’ road win changed the early-season picture for both teams: the Wolves improved to 4–1, and Clarksdale took its first defeat. The Wildcats finished with 17 points in the nonconference meeting, while Cleveland Central’s 32 were enough to send the visiting team home with the victory.

The boys game also went to Cleveland Central, 41–34, with the fourth quarter supplying the decisive separation. The Wolves outscored Clarksdale 16–6 in the final period after scoring eight, nine and eight points in the opening three quarters. Cleveland Central moved to 2–3; the Wildcats fell to 0–5.

Rosa Fort stays perfect; Edwards and Coahoma County split

Rosa Fort’s boys faced a road test at Riverside and left with a 68–22 nonconference win. The Lions’ unbeaten record now stands at 4–0, while the Bulldogs are 2–5. The Lions were among the unbeaten teams featured in Wednesday’s Games To Watch preview, which also featured Cleveland Central’s girls and the MRA and Heritage soccer matches.

Edwards’ boys won 49–38 at Coahoma County in another meeting between teams with winning records. The Tigers improved to 4–2, while the Panthers’ postgame mark is 3–2. The nonconference result adds a road win to Edwards’ early-season schedule.

Coahoma County took the girls game 44–32, ensuring the schools split the varsity basketball results. The Panthers are 3–4 after the win, and Edwards is 1–5.

Unbeaten soccer starts continue at MRA and Heritage

MRA’s 2–0 home win over Bayou Academy carried conference significance as well as extending its unbeaten opening. The Patriots are 2–0 overall after keeping the Colts off the scoreboard; Bayou Academy’s record is 1–2. The match listing identifies it as a conference contest.

Heritage Academy needed only one goal to preserve its perfect start against Washington. The 1–0 nonconference victory put the Patriots at 4–0. Washington’s reported record is 0–1 after the trip to Columbus.

Delta Streets Academy also won at home, beating Regents 2–1 in Greenwood. All the scoring came in the first half: DSA scored twice and Regents once, with neither team adding a second-half goal. DSA is 3–2, while Regents’ reported record is 0–1.

River Oaks builds early lead against Newton County Academy

In football, Newton County Academy lost 36–6 at River Oaks in Monroe, Louisiana. River Oaks scored eight points in the first quarter, 20 in the second and eight in the third; the Generals’ six points came in the fourth. The game page identifies the contest as a playoff game and lists River Oaks at 12–1 and Newton County Academy at 10–5 afterward.
